title: Choose the visual world for Growing Minds Science
question: The roll assigned The Growth Chart. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every card carries the product's real content; the sketch is the first viewport's composition, not its finish.

options.label: The Growth Chart
options.lineage: the pediatric growth chart every parent has held
options.thesis: The whole page is one chart of the first five years, and the classes are its x-axis; the science is plotted, never pictured.
options.viewport: A chalk-white grid fills the viewport edge to edge. Three developmental curves (language, self-regulation, executive function) sweep across it at architectural scale. The headline sits inside the chart plane, upper left, with the lede and a filled teal action beneath. A vermilion age cursor stands at 2 yrs 3 mo with a live readout of what is growing now. The bottom axis is the curriculum: four age ranges, each a class with its lesson count and price.
options.risk: Reads as a clinic chart if any child is ever plotted against a norm; the chart must always show what grows, never where a child falls.

raised.raise: The headline owns the chart plane at architectural scale instead of sitting in a text column.
State rides the grid itself: lines tighten toward the age cursor and relax elsewhere, so attention is drawn without a second colour.
Every control has a drawn state: pressed inverts to ink, disabled dims to a dotted grid, the chosen class fills its axis cell.
Text is banded in courses, each line's measure matching its band, so dense content reads as the chart's own strata.

options.label: The Lab Frame
options.lineage: the developmental lab's coded video frame
options.thesis: A real ordinary moment fills the frame and the science annotates it in the margin, so the parent learns to see what their child is doing.
options.viewport: A photograph of a parent and toddler fills the left 900px, headline set on it in a sturdy grotesk, a timecode at the foot. A white margin on the right carries three ruled, timecoded codes (Serve, Return, Joint attention) with vermilion leaders pointing into the frame, then the lede and a filled ink action.
options.risk: Also where most runs in this category land: a big photo hero. It lives or dies on the annotations being true observations, not decoration, and on the photography being the site's own.

options.label: The Daylight Section
options.lineage: the architect's daylight section through a family home
options.thesis: The page is a section cut through your home, and the science is pinned where the day's light lands: breakfast, nap, bath, bedtime.
options.viewport: Charcoal section-cut walls frame three rooms across the full width on limewash ground. A gold beam enters the upper-right room and lands on the breakfast table, stamped 08:12 in tabular numerals, with an annotation naming what is developmentally happening and which class teaches it. The headline sits in the white of the big room in inclined lettering, the lede under it, and the action is a gold plaque on the wall. A time rail across the foot (06:40 wake to 19:45 bedtime) is the navigation; dragging the hour moves the beam through the house.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: parents live in that house and that day, and the moments where the science applies are literally the hours on the rail. Beats the chart on identification (home over clinic) and on clarity (what to do at 08:12 is the product).
options.risk: An architectural drawing can read as an architect's site; every annotation must be about the parent and child, and the beam must do work (carry the hour and the class), not decorate.

options.label: The Darkroom
options.lineage: a printing darkroom under amber safelight
options.thesis: Understanding develops like a print: lesson by lesson a clearer picture of your child emerges in the tray.
options.viewport: Amber-washed dark ground. Headline left in bold grotesk, lede and a safelight-gold action beneath. On the right a white enamel tray holds a print mid-development; a timer reads 00:48 beneath it. A six-step test strip bands the foot of the viewport. Scrolling develops the print.
options.case: Holds identification: the lamp-lit evening after bedtime is this audience's real scene. Loses clarity: a dark amber ground is the incumbent's own move at night, and the offer reads dimmer than it should.
options.risk: Reads as the current site after dark; the development reveal must be the page's mechanism, not a screen effect.

options.label: The Street Poster
options.thesis: The wall shouts the class names in wood-type capitals.
options.viewport: Stacked condensed capitals cropped by the frame, one red-orange band for the action.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a tired parent does not identify with a shouting wall, and all-caps cropped words hide the offer.
options.kept: Type at architectural scale that owns its viewport.

options.label: The Moiré Gallery
options.thesis: Attention generated optically by line frequency alone.
options.viewport: Wave canvases in white margins, one caption each.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an overstimulating field is the opposite of what a stressed parent needs, and it carries no science.
options.kept: State carried by the pattern itself, not by an added colour.

options.label: The One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: Every tone a dither, every state a drawn pixel.
options.viewport: Overlapping windows on one desktop plane.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nostalgia for a computer the audience never used, and the offer reads as a toy.
options.kept: Every control state has a drawn form; nothing is implied by colour alone.

options.label: The Coiled Tower
options.thesis: Development as courses laid one on another.
options.viewport: Text banded in horizontal courses rising up the page.
options.case: Fuses weakly: parents do not identify with ceramics, though courses map to modules.
options.kept: Text banded in courses with the measure matching the band.
options.risk: Terracotta on cream is the spent default.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What parenting-class sites ship, executed impeccably: a warm photograph, a rounded teal button, three proof cards.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and lede left, a rounded photograph of a parent and child right, two pill buttons, three icon cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other parenting course by design.
